kjv: and blesseth the covetous, [whom] the LORD abhorreth
mine: and the one greedy for gain curses and renounces Yahweh
note: uvotsea' berekh ni'ets yhwh: botsea' is most naturally the subject ("the greedy man"), and berekh "bless" is the scribal euphemism for "curse" (as in Job 1:5) paired with ni'ets "spurns"; the KJV makes the wicked bless the greedy and God abhor them. Context: the greedy man curses and renounces Yahweh (low confidence). Ni'ets with God as object recurs in 10:13 ('why does the wicked renounce God?'), so 'renounces Yahweh' is secure. Barakh is unsettled: 'curses' (scribal euphemism, as Job 1:5; 1 Kgs 21:10) with the greedy man as subject (ESV, NASB, NRSV, NJPS), or the wicked 'blesses the greedy' (NIV, CSB, NET). Other possible meanings: (1) 'he blesses the greedy and spurns Yahweh' — NIV, CSB, NET; (2) 'the greedy man blesses himself', i.e. boasts — some commentators; (3) 'blesses the covetous, whom Yahweh abhors', Yahweh as subject — KJV (less likely given 10:13); (4) 'the unjust man is blessed' — LXX, Vulgate.
